title: Japan's Prime Minister Resigned After 69 Days For Being Too Cheap
description: AI-narrated commentary on Japan's Prime Minister Sōsuke Uno, who resigned after just 69 days in office in 1989 following a geisha scandal, not for the affair itself, but for how little he paid her. Original commentary, not sourced from any single video.

hook_candidates.text: A Japanese Prime Minister resigned after 69 days, for being too cheap to his mistress.
Everyone assumes a political affair scandal ends a career because of the cheating. This one didn't.
What if a Prime Minister's affair wasn't what ended his career, but how he paid for it?
A geisha named Mitsuko Nakanishi ended a sitting Prime Minister's career, by revealing exactly how little he paid her.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks any affair scandal is just about the cheating, because they want to prove this one was about something pettier.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a Prime Minister only resigns for having an affair, not for being cheap.
closing_comment: Resigning in 69 days for being cheap might be the pettiest downfall a Prime Minister has ever had.

sources.note: 1989 wire report: geisha Nakanishi described the affair and the ~300,000 yen/month arrangement with PM Uno.
Contemporary 1989 report on the election losses that pushed PM Uno toward resignation after 69 days.
